Yechezkel's Temple precinct over today's Jerusalem

Chapter 42, verses 15 to 20. Four sides of 500 reeds each, a reed being six amot: a wall 3,000 amot square, about 1.44 km a side at the 48 cm amah you approved. Drawn on the OpenStreetMap street map; north is up.

Yechezkel's wall, 3,000 amotTemple courts as builtSecond Temple Har HaBayit, Middot 2:1, 500 amot

Orange is the wall Yechezkel measures in chapter 42, verses 15 to 20: he is led outside the Temple compound and each of its four sides is measured at 500 reeds, a reed being six amot. That is 3,000 amot a side, about 1.44 km at your 48 cm amah. Blue is the Temple court platform exactly where the build has it. Dashed blue is the Second Temple's Har HaBayit from Middot 2:1, 500 amot square, for scale: Yechezkel's precinct is six times the side and thirty-six times the area.

Where it lands. Your book follows Mishkenei Elyon in putting the Temple near the north-west of the precinct, 500 amot in from the west and north walls, so the square runs mostly east and south. Inside it: the whole Temple Mount, the eastern Muslim Quarter, the Jewish Quarter out to about 170 m west of the Kotel, the Kidron valley, the slope of the Mount of Olives, the City of David and Silwan. About 1,900 of today's buildings stand within the line. West of it the Old City continues untouched.

The Aron. The gold dot is the Aron in the Kodesh HaKodashim. The build already places it over the Dome of the Rock: the dome centre is 63 m west of the court centre and the Aron is at 62 m, one metre apart, inside the four-metre uncertainty of where the exposed rock lies within the dome. The rock itself is about 13.6 m below the Temple floor as built.
